components.gap: The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.model-density-invariance is not supplied for one promised case. The entry asserts (body lines 136-137) 'Declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is not such a transport in general', but the declared proof (annex lines 97-104) proves only the positive pushforward invariance of m_k(x) and then restates the negative ('not under an arbitrary reassignment of a coordinate density') with no argument and no counterexample. Neither the entry nor its proof cites the uniform-prior/theta-squared counterexample that exists separately at handbook/parts/p15/bayesian-updating-prediction.tex lines 313-318. Failure condition 'missing promised direction/case' therefore holds for this sentence. The other claims of the entry are proved at annex lines 59-113, and the worked boundary is at body 148-155 / annex 115-119.

defect_observations.observation: Unproved negative claim (the basis of the partial verdict). The flat-prior sentence at body 136-137 gets no argument. Adding or citing a counterexample would close it, for example uniform theta on (0,1) with eta=theta^2, whose pushforward density is 1/(2 sqrt eta) (bayesian-updating-prediction.tex 313-318).

Minor terseness, not counted as a gap. The proof asserts that {sum_k alpha_k r_k > 0} has full Q_alpha-mass without the one-line reason (Q_alpha has Q_*-density sum_k alpha_k r_k). The extension of the r_k description to an arbitrary alternative dominating measure is compressed into one sentence invoking RN uniqueness.

Borderline, accepted. 'No equality of nuisance priors in different models is automatic' gets no argument in annex 124-157. I accepted it as following from the definition, where each H_k supplies its own Pi_k, together with the null-constraint version example of C011 (annex 360-375). A stricter reader could ask for an explicit pointer.

Implicit step, accepted. The unrestricted proper-prior bound moves from the pointwise likelihood bound 1/sqrt(2 pi s^2) to the marginal-likelihood bound without restating that a prior average cannot exceed the maximum. That inequality is written in the same annex at lines 144-146.

Notation clash with the held source, not counted against any listed exact entry. Here alpha_k denotes model prior probabilities. K&R eq. (16), p. 784, which body line 11 cites, uses alpha_k for the prior odds pr(H_k)/pr(H_0) with alpha_0=1 and gives pr(H_k|D)=alpha_k B_k0 / sum_r alpha_r B_r0. The chapter neither states that form nor flags the different meaning of alpha_k. Reviewers should check whether the scope record (not opened, per rules) identifies eq. (16) as a variant to preserve.

Source nuance not reproduced, and not owed by the exact entry texts. K&R Sec. 5.1 (p. 781) says the conditional specification pi(beta|H0)=pi(beta|psi=psi0,H1) depends on the parameterization (Borel paradox). The chapter states that the two specifications must be justified and gives a version-nonuniqueness example (C011), but does not mention the parameterization dependence.
